original_value: Smart health (s-health) is a vital topic and an essential research field today, supporting the real-time monitoring of user’s data by using sensors, either in direct or indirect contact with the human body. Real-time monitoring promotes changes in healthcare from a reactive to a proactive paradigm, contributing to early detection, prevention, and long-term management of health conditions. Under these new conditions, continuous user authentication plays a key role in protecting data and access control, once it focuses on keeping track of a user’s identity throughout the system operation. Traditional user authentication systems cannot fulfill the security requirements of s-health, because they are limited, prone to security breaches, and require the user to frequently authenticate by, e.g., a password or fingerprint. This interrupts the normal use of the system, being highly inconvenient and not user friendly. Also, data transmission in current authentication systems relies on wireless technologies, which are susceptible to eavesdropping during the pairing stage. Biological signals, e.g., electrocardiogram (ECG) and electroencephalogram (EEG), can offer continuous and seamless authentication bolstered by exclusive characteristics from each individual. However, it is necessary to redesign current authentication systems to encompass biometric traits and new communication technologies that can jointly protect data and provide continuous authentication. Hence, this article presents a novel biosignal authentication system, in which the photoplethysmogram (PPG) biosignal and a galvanic coupling (GC) channel lead to continuous, seamless, and secure user authentication. Furthermore, this article contributes to a clear organization of the state of the art on biosignal-based continuous user authentication systems, assisting research studies in this field. The evaluation of the system feasibility presents accuracy in keeping data integrity and up to 98.66% accuracy in the authentication process.

result.paraphrase: Smart health (s-health) is an important topic and a key research area today, enabling real-time monitoring of user data through sensors in direct or indirect contact with the human body. Such monitoring shifts healthcare from a reactive model to a proactive one, helping with early detection, prevention, and long-term management of health conditions. In this context, continuous user authentication is crucial for data protection and access control because it tracks a user’s identity throughout system operation. Conventional authentication methods are not adequate for s-health security requirements, as they are limited, vulnerable to security breaches, and force users to authenticate repeatedly, for example with a password or fingerprint. This disrupts normal system use and is highly inconvenient and not user friendly. Moreover, data transmission in existing authentication systems depends on wireless technologies that are vulnerable to eavesdropping during pairing. Biological signals such as electrocardiogram (ECG) and electroencephalogram (EEG) can provide continuous, seamless authentication thanks to each person’s unique characteristics. Even so, current authentication systems must be redesigned to incorporate biometric traits and new communication technologies that together protect data and enable continuous authentication. Accordingly, this article introduces a new biosignal authentication system where photoplethysmogram (PPG) biosignals and a galvanic coupling (GC) channel enable continuous, seamless, and secure user authentication. It also offers a clear organization of the state of the art in biosignal-based continuous user authentication systems, supporting research in this area. Feasibility evaluation shows data integrity accuracy and authentication accuracy of up to 98.66%.
